sentences.tr: fa-qālū innanā naḥnu banātu mulūkin wa-naḥnu mujtami'īna hunā muddata sinīna naghību arba'īna yawman wa-naq'udu sanatan na'kulu wa-nashrabu wa-nalladhdhu wa-naṭrabu thumma naghību wa-hādhā da'bunā
sentences.l: So they said: indeed-we, we, [are] daughters-of kings, and-we [are] gathered here [for] a-space-of years; we-are-absent forty a-day, and-we-stay a-year, we-eat and-we-drink and-we-take-pleasure and-we-make-merry, then we-are-absent; and-this [is] our-custom.
sentences.i: So they said, “We are, in truth, daughters of kings, and we have been gathered here for years now: we go away for forty days and settle in for a year, eating, drinking, taking our pleasure and making merry; then we go away again—this is our custom.”
sentences.n: "مُجْتَمِعِينَ" carries the sound-plural ending -īna (visible in the rasm, مجتمعين) even though, functioning as predicate of نحن, Classical grammar would call for the nominative مُجْتَمِعُونَ. Kept as the text has it, a Middle-Arabic collapse of the case distinction rather than an error to silently fix.

sentences.t: وَنَخْشَى أَنَّكَ تُخَالِفُنَا بَعْدَ أَنْ نَغِيبَ عَنْكَ فِيمَا نَأْمُرُكَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-nakhshā annaka tukhālifunā ba'da an naghība 'anka fīmā na'muruka bihi
sentences.l: And we-fear that-you will-oppose-us, after that we-are-absent from-you, in-what we-command-you with-it.
sentences.i: And we fear that you will go against us, once we are away from you, in what we charge you with.

sentences.t: فَهَا نَحْنُ نُسَلِّمُ إِلَيْكَ مَفَاتِيحَ الْقَصْرِ وَفِيهِ أَرْبَعُونَ خِزَانَةً
sentences.tr: fa-hā naḥnu nusallimu ilayka mafātīḥa al-qaṣri wa-fīhi arba'ūna khizānatan
sentences.l: So here we are, handing-over to-you the-keys-of the-palace; and-in-it [are] forty a-storeroom.
sentences.i: So here we are, handing you the keys of the palace; in it are forty storerooms.

sentences.t: فَأَنْتَ تَفْتَحُ هَٰذِهِ التِّسْعَةَ وَثَلٰثِينَ بَابًا وَ الْحَذَرَ أَنْ تَفْتَحَ الْبَابَ الْأَرْبَعِينَ فَتُفَارِقَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-anta taftaḥu hādhihi al-tis'ata wa-thalāthīna bāban wa-al-ḥadhara an taftaḥa al-bāba al-arba'īna fa-tufāriqanā
sentences.l: So you may-open these thirty-nine a-door; and-beware! that you-open the-door the-fortieth, lest-you-be-parted-from-us.
sentences.i: So you may open these thirty-nine doors, but beware of opening the fortieth door, or you will be parted from us.
sentences.n: "الْحَذَرَ" is the accusative of warning (تحذير): an implied verb of caution is dropped and only its object survives, giving the force of an exclamation, "Beware!" "ثَلٰثِينَ" is printed ثلثين, without the medial alif of ثلاثين; the missing long ā is supplied with the dagger alif rather than by inserting a letter the archive does not have.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ لَا أَفْتَحُهُ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ مُفَارَقَتُكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahum lā aftaḥuhu in kāna fīhi mufāraqatukum
sentences.l: So I said to them: I-will-not open-it, if there-was in-it your-parting.
sentences.i: So I said to them, “I will never open it, if it means parting from you.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَتْ مِنْهُنَّ وَاحِدَةٌ وَعَانَقَتْنِي وَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma taqaddamat minhunna wāḥidatun wa-'ānaqatnī wa-bakat wa-qālat shi'ran
sentences.l: Then came-forward from-among-them one (f.), and-she-embraced-me and-wept and-said, in-verse:
sentences.i: Then one of them came forward, embraced me, wept, and said in verse:

sentences.t:
لَئِنْ ضَمَّنَا بَعْدَ التَّنَائِي تَقَرُّبٌ * تَبَسَّمَ وَجْهُ الدَّهْرِ بَعْدَ قُطُوبِهِ
وَإِنْ كَحَلَتْ عَيْنَايَ مِنْكُمْ بِنَظْرَةٍ * غَفَرْتُ لِدَهْرِي سَالِفَاتِ ذُنُوبِهِ
sentences.tr:
la'in ḍammanā ba'da al-tanā'ī taqarrubun * tabassama wajhu al-dahri ba'da quṭūbihi
wa-in kaḥalat 'aynāya minkum bi-naẓratin * ghafartu li-dahrī sālifāti dhunūbihi
sentences.l:
If indeed a-drawing-near joined-us after the-estrangement * the-face-of Time smiled after its-frown
and-if my-two-eyes were-kohled by-you with-a-glance * I-forgave to-my-Time its-past sins
sentences.i: If, after our estrangement, a closeness should bring us together, Time's own face will smile after its frown; and if my eyes were lined with kohl by a single glance of yours, I would forgive Time all its past offences.
sentences.n: "تَقَرُّبٌ" is read as the delayed subject of ضَمَّنَا ("a drawing-near joined us"), with "نا" as its object—the ordinary word order for this kind of balanced verse clause.

sentences.t: أَيْضًا وَأَنْشَلَتْ
sentences.tr: ayḍan wa-anshalat
sentences.l: Also, and she [anshalat]—
sentences.i: And she recited further—
sentences.n: "وَأَنْشَلَتْ", read by its letters, would be from ن-ش-ل ("to snatch/pull out"), which does not fit; introducing a further verse quotation, the sense clearly wants وَأَنْشَدَتْ, "and she recited [more verse]" (أَنْشَدَ شِعْرًا is the standard phrase). This is the same د/ل substitution as "أَرْغَل" above and "وَجِلْتُ" below. Kept as printed, translated for the intended sense.

sentences.t:
وَلَمَّا تَدَانَتْ لِلْفِرَاقِ وَقَلْبُهُمَا * حَلِيفَانِ يَوْمًا لِلصَّبَابَةِ وَالْوَجْدَا
بَكَتْ لُؤْلُؤًا رَطْبًا وَفَاضَتْ مَدَامِعِي * عَقِيقًا فَصَارَ الْكُلُّ فِي نَحْرِهَا عِقْدًا
sentences.tr:
wa-lammā tadānat li-al-firāqi wa-qalbuhumā * ḥalīfāni yawman li-al-ṣabābati wa-al-wajdā
bakat lu'lu'an raṭban wa-fāḍat madāmi'ī * 'aqīqan fa-ṣāra al-kullu fī naḥrihā 'iqdan
sentences.l:
And when she drew near to the-parting, and-their-two-hearts * [were] two-allies, one day, to-passion and-yearning,
she wept moist pearls, and-overflowed my-tears * carnelian, and-the-whole became, on her-throat, a-necklace.
sentences.i: And when she drew close for the parting—our two hearts being, for that day, allies bound to passion and longing—she wept fresh pearls, and my own tears overflowed as carnelian, and all of it became, upon her throat, a single necklace.
sentences.n: "الْوَجْدَا" carries a poetic alif of prolongation (itlāq) added purely for the rhyme, not a case-ending; the underlying word is الوَجْد.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُ بُكَاهَا قُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَفْتَحُهُ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ra'aytu bukāhā qultu wa-Allāhi lā aftaḥuhu abadan
sentences.l: So when I-saw her-weeping, I-said: by-God, I-will-not open-it, ever.
sentences.i: So when I saw her weeping, I said, “By God, I will never open it.”

sentences.t: وَوَدَّعْتُهَا وَخَرَجُوا ثُمَّ طَارُوا
sentences.tr: wa-wadda'tuhā wa-kharajū thumma ṭārū
sentences.l: And I-bade-her-farewell, and-they went-out, then they-flew.
sentences.i: And I bade her farewell, and they went out, then they flew away.

sentences.t: فَقَعَدْتُ فِى الْقَصْرِ وَحْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qa'adtu fī al-qaṣri waḥdī
sentences.l: So I-sat in the-palace, alone-of-me.
sentences.i: So I sat in the palace, alone.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا قَرُبَ الْمَسَاءُ فَتَحْتُ الْخِزَانَةَ الْأُولَى وَدَخَلْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lammā qaruba al-masā'u fataḥtu al-khizānata al-ūlā wa-dakhaltuhā
sentences.l: And when drew-near the-evening, I-opened the-storeroom the-first, and-I-entered-it.
sentences.i: And when evening drew near, I opened the first storeroom and went in.

sentences.t: فَوَجِلْتُ فِيهَا بَيْتًا كَأَنَّهُ الْجَنَّةُ وَفِيهِ بُسْتَانٌ أَشْجَارُهُ مُخْضَرَّةٌ وَثِمَارُهُ يَانِعَةٌ وَأَطْيَارُهُ صَادِحَةٌ وَمِيَاهُهُ مُتَدَفِّقَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-wajiltu fīhā baytan ka'annahu al-jannatu wa-fīhi bustānun ashjāruhu mukhḍarratun wa-thimāruhu yāni'atun wa-aṭyāruhu ṣādiḥatun wa-miyāhuhu mutadaffiqatun
sentences.l: So I-[wajiltu] in-it a-chamber as-though-it [were] the-Paradise; and-in-it a-garden, its-trees green, and-its-fruits ripe, and-its-birds singing, and-its-waters flowing.
sentences.i: So I [found] in it a chamber like Paradise itself: in it was a garden, its trees green, its fruit ripe, its birds singing, its waters running free.
sentences.n: "فَوَجِلْتُ", by its letters, is from و-ج-ل ("to fear"): "so I feared—" makes no sense with a direct object following. The sense wanted is plainly فَوَجَدْتُ, "so I found", the same د/ل substitution noted at "أَرْغَل" and "أَنْشَلَتْ" above (contrast the correctly-spelled فَوَجَدْتُ later in this night, at the second storeroom). Kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَارْتَاحَ بِهَا خَاطِرِي
sentences.tr: fa-irtāḥa bihā khāṭirī
sentences.l: So found-rest in-it my-mind.
sentences.i: And my mind found ease in it.

sentences.t: وَتَمَشَّيْتُ بَيْنَ الْأَشْجَارِ وَشَمَمْتُ رَوَائِحَ الْأَزْهَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-tamashshaytu bayna al-ashjāri wa-shamamtu rawā'iḥa al-azhāri
sentences.l: And I-walked among the-trees, and-I-smelled the-scents-of the-flowers,
sentences.i: And I walked among the trees, and breathed in the scent of the flowers,

sentences.t: وَسَمِعْتُ غِنَاءَ الْأَطْيَارِ وَهِيَ تُسَبِّحُ الْوَاحِدَ الْقَهَّارَ
sentences.tr: wa-sami'tu ghinā'a al-aṭyāri wa-hiya tusabbiḥu al-wāḥida al-qahhāra
sentences.l: and-I-heard the-singing-of the-birds while-they glorify the-One, the-All-Compelling.
sentences.i: and heard the birds singing as they glorified the One, the All-Compelling.

sentences.t: وَرَأَيْتُ لَوْنَ التُّفَّاحِ بَيْنَ اِحْمِرَارٍ وَ تُفَّاحَةً جَمَعَتْ لَوْنَيْنِ خِلْقَتُهَا عِنْدَ الْحَبِيبِ لَوْنُ الصَّائِمِ الْوَجِلِ
sentences.tr: wa-ra'aytu lawna al-tuffāḥi bayna iḥmirārin wa-tuffāḥatan jama'at lawnayni khilqatuhā 'inda al-ḥabībi lawnu al-ṣā'imi al-wajili
sentences.l: And I-saw the-color-of the-apples amid a-redness, and-an-apple [that] combined two-colors: its-hue, with the-beloved, [is] the-color-of the-fasting-one, the-anxious-one.
sentences.i: And I saw the apples ranging in redness, and an apple that combined two colors, whose hue—to the beloved's eye—is the color of the anxious man fasting: pale and flushed at once.
sentences.n: The apple of “two colors” (pale and red together) is a stock image for the face of a lover made anxious before the beloved—pallor from fasting/love-sickness, a flush from fear or shame. "عِنْدَ الْحَبِيبِ" is taken as “in the beloved's eyes/estimation” rather than literally “next to the beloved”; the syntax of خِلْقَتُهَا...لَوْنُ is compressed and admits more than one parsing.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرْتُ إِلَى السَّفَرْجَلِ وَاسْتَرْوَحْتُ عَرْفَهُ الْمُزْرِيَ بِرَائِحَةِ الْمِسْكِ وَ الْعَنْبَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓartu ilā al-safarjali wa-istarwaḥtu 'arfahu al-muzriya bi-rā'iḥati al-miski wa-al-'anbari
sentences.l: Then I-looked at the-quince, and-I-caught-the-scent-of its-fragrance, the-shaming, [as compared] with-the-scent-of the-musk and-the-ambergris,
sentences.i: Then I looked at the quince, and breathed in its fragrance—a scent that puts musk and ambergris to shame,

sentences.t: وَهُوَ لِمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ وَأَخْبَرَ —
sentences.tr: wa-huwa li-mā qāla al-shā'iru wa-akhbara —
sentences.l: and it [is] as-to-what the-poet said and-told—
sentences.i: and it is just as the poet has said and told—
sentences.n: "لِمَا" is read here as “concerning/as to what” (introducing the coming verse-quotation about the quince), rather than the temporal لَمَّا “when”, which has no clause to attach to here.

sentences.t:
حَازَ السَّفَرْجَلُ لَذَّاتِ الْوَرَى فَغَدَا * عَلَى الْفَوَاكِهِ بِالتَّفْضِيلِ مَشْهُورًا
كَالرَّاحِ طَعْمًا وَنَشْرُ الْمِسْكِ رَائِحَةً * وَالتِّبْرُ لَوْنًا وَشَكْلُ الْبَدْرِ تَنْوِيرًا
sentences.tr:
ḥāza al-safarjalu ladhdhāti al-warā fa-ghadā * 'alā al-fawākihi bi-al-tafḍīli mashhūran
ka-al-rāḥi ṭa'man wa-nashru al-miski rā'iḥatan * wa-al-tibru lawnan wa-shaklu al-badri tanwīran
sentences.l:
The-quince has-attained the-pleasures-of mankind, and-it-became * over the-fruits, in-excellence, renowned:
like the-wine in-taste, and-the-diffusion-of the-musk in-scent, * and-the-gold in-color, and-the-shape-of the-full-moon in-radiance.
sentences.i: The quince has won the delight of all mankind, and become renowned above every fruit for its excellence: in taste like wine, in scent like musk's own fragrance, in color like gold, and in radiance like the shape of the full moon.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرْتُ إِلَى بُرْقُوقٍ يَرُوقُ الْعَيْنَ حُسْنُهُ كَأَنَّهُ يَاقُوتٌ مَخْلُوقٌ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓartu ilā burqūqin yarūqu al-'ayna ḥusnuhu ka'annahu yāqūtun makhlūqun
sentences.l: Then I-looked at plums, whose-beauty delights the-eye, as-though-it [were] a-ruby, created.
sentences.i: Then I looked at plums whose beauty delights the eye, as though they were rubies freshly made.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ مِنْ ذَٰلِكَ الْمَكَانِ وَأَغْلَقْتُ بَابَ الْخِزَانَةِ كَمَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajtu min dhālika al-makāni wa-aghlaqtu bāba al-khizānati kamā kāna
sentences.l: Then I-left from that the-place, and-I-closed the-door-of the-storeroom, as it-was.
sentences.i: Then I left that place, and closed the storeroom door as it had been.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ فَتَحْتُ خِزَانَةً أُخْرَى وَدَخَلْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lammā kāna al-ghadu fataḥtu khizānatan ukhrā wa-dakhaltuhā
sentences.l: And when came the-morrow, I-opened a-storeroom, another, and-I-entered-it,
sentences.i: And when the next day came, I opened another storeroom and went in,

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ فِيهَا مَيْدَانًا كَبِيرًا وَفِيهِ نَخْلٌ كَبِيرٌ وَنَهْرٌ جَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu fīhā maydānan kabīran wa-fīhi nakhlun kabīrun wa-nahrun jārin
sentences.l: so-I-found in-it a-great open-ground, and-in-it tall palm-trees and-a-river flowing,
sentences.i: and found in it a great open ground, with tall palms and a flowing river,

sentences.t: وَأَشْجَارُ الْوَرْدِ وَالْيَاسَمِينِ وَالْبَرَدَقُوشِ وَالنَّسْرِينِ وَالنَّرْجِسِ وَالْمَنْشُورِ مَفْرُوشَةٌ بِحَافَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ashjāru al-wardi wa-al-yāsamīni wa-al-baradaqūshi wa-al-nasrīni wa-al-narjisi wa-al-manshūri mafrūshatun bi-ḥāfatihi
sentences.l: and trees-of rose and-jasmine and-marjoram and-eglantine and-narcissus and-al-manshūr, spread along-its-edge.
sentences.i: and trees of rose, jasmine, marjoram, eglantine, narcissus and manshūr-flowers carpeting its bank.
sentences.n: "الْمَنْشُورِ" (literally “the spread-out/published one”) is very likely a misprint for المَنْثُور (with thā', not shīn), a real flower conventionally paired with narcissus in garden descriptions (“النرجس والمنثور” is a standard phrase); the two letters are easy to confuse on the page. Kept exactly as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَلَّ هَبَّتِ الرِّيَاحُ عَلَى تِلْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qalla habbati al-riyāḥu 'alā tilka
sentences.l: And seldom did-blow the-winds upon those—
sentences.i: And seldom did the wind blow upon those—
sentences.n: "وَقَلَّ" is read as qalla (“it was rare/little”, i.e. “seldom”), not as the defective spelling of قَالَ (“he said”) that this edition elsewhere shows, since no reported speech follows here—only “the winds blew”. The sentence continues past this point; the noun that "تِلْكَ" refers to lies beyond it, in the next archived line.

sentences.t: اَلرَّيَاحِينِ فَانْتَشَرَ ذَلِكَ اَلطِّيبُ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا وَحَصَلَ لِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ اَلسُّرُورُ اَلتَّامُّ
sentences.tr: al-rayāḥīni fa-intashara dhālika l-ṭību yamīnan wa-shimālan wa-ḥaṣala lī min dhālika l-surūru l-tāmmu
sentences.l: ...the sweet basils, and that perfume spread right and left, and there came to me from that the complete joy.
sentences.i: ...the sweet basils, and their fragrance spread out on every side, and I felt complete joy from it.
sentences.n: This excerpt opens mid-sentence, continuing a list of aromatic plants from just before it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَكَانِ وَأَغْلَقْتُ بَابَ اَلْخِزَانَةِ كَمَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajtu min dhālika l-makāni wa-aghlaqtu bāba l-khizānati kamā kāna
sentences.l: Then I went out from that place, and I closed the door of the storeroom as it had been.
sentences.i: Then I left that place and shut the storeroom door behind me, just as it had been.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فَتَحْتُ بَابَ اَلْخِزَانَةِ اَلثَّالِثَةِ فَرَأَيْتُ فِيهِ قَاعَةً كَبِيرَةً مَفْرُوشَةً بِالرُّخَامِ اَلْمُلَوَّنِ وَالْمَعَادِنِ اَلْمُثَمَّنَةِ وَالأَحْجَارِ اَلْفَاخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma fataḥtu bāba l-khizānati l-thālithati fa-ra'aytu fīhi qāʿatan kabīratan mafrūshatan bi-al-rukhāmi l-mulawwani wa-al-maʿādini l-muthammanati wa-al-aḥjāri l-fākhirati
sentences.l: Then I opened the door of the third storeroom, and I saw in it a great hall, spread with colored marble, and precious metals, and splendid stones.
sentences.i: Then I opened the door of the third storeroom, and inside I found a great hall floored with colored marble, precious metals, and magnificent gems.

sentences.t: وَفِيهَا أَقْفَاصٌ مِنْ اَلصَّنْدَلِ وَالْعُودِ فِيهَا طُيُورٌ تُغَنِّي مِثْلَ اَلْهَزَارِ وَالْمُطَوَّقِ وَالشُّحْرُورِ وَالْقُمْرِيِّ وَالنُّوبِيِّ اَلْمُغَرِّدِ
sentences.tr: wa-fīhā aqfāṣun min al-ṣandali wa-al-ʿūdi fīhā ṭuyūrun tughannī mithla l-hazāri wa-al-muṭawwaqi wa-al-shuḥrūri wa-al-qumriyyi wa-al-nūbiyyi l-mugharridi
sentences.l: And in it were cages of sandalwood and aloeswood, in them birds singing, like the nightingale and the ring-dove and the blackbird and the turtledove and the melodious Nubian dove.
sentences.i: And in it were cages of sandalwood and aloeswood, with birds singing inside them — nightingale, ring-dove, blackbird, turtledove, and the sweet-voiced Nubian dove.

sentences.t: فَطَابَ قَلْبِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَ اِنْفَرَجَ هَمِّي وَنِمْتُ فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْمَكَانِ إِلَى اَلصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭāba qalbī min dhālika wa infaraja hammī wa-nimtu fī dhālika l-makāni ilā l-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And my heart grew sweet from that, and my care was loosened, and I slept in that place until morning.
sentences.i: And my heart was gladdened by it, my worries eased, and I slept there until morning.
sentences.n: The archive prints و alone at the line's end here (and at four more points below), with the word it belongs to starting the next line; kept as the archive's own separate word-token rather than silently rejoined.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فَتَحْتُ بَابَ اَلْخِزَانَةِ اَلرَّابِعَةِ فَوَجَدْتُ فِيهَا بَيْتًا كَبِيرًا وَفِي ذَلِكَ اَلْبَيْتِ أَرْبَعِينَ خِزَانَةً مُفَتَّحَةَ اَلأَبْوَابِ
sentences.tr: thumma fataḥtu bāba l-khizānati l-rābiʿati fa-wajadtu fīhā baytan kabīran wa-fī dhālika l-bayti arbaʿīna khizānatan mufattaḥata l-abwābi
sentences.l: Then I opened the door of the fourth storeroom, and I found in it a great chamber, and in that chamber were forty compartments, their doors open.
sentences.i: Then I opened the door of the fourth storeroom and found inside a great chamber, and within it were forty compartments standing open.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْتُ فِيهِمْ فَرَأَيْتُ مِنَ اللُّؤْلُؤِ وَالْيَاقُوتِ وَالزَّبَرْجَلِ وَالزُّمُرُّذِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ اَلنَّفِيسَةِ مَا لَا يُوصَفُ بِلِسَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhaltu fīhim fa-ra'aytu mina l-lu'lu'i wa-al-yāqūti wa-al-zabarjali wa-al-zumurrudhi wa-al-jawāhiri l-nafīsati mā lā yūṣafu bi-lisānin
sentences.l: So I entered among them, and I saw, of pearl and ruby and zabarjal and zumurrudh and precious gems, what cannot be described by any tongue.
sentences.i: So I went in among them, and saw such pearls, rubies, chrysolite, emerald, and other precious gems as no tongue could describe.
sentences.n: The archive spells 'chrysolite' الزبرجل and 'emerald' الزمرذ (for the expected زبرجد, زمرد); kept as printed, letters unaltered.

sentences.t: فَاندَهَشَ عَقْلِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-indahasha ʿaqlī min dhālika
sentences.l: And my mind was astonished at that.
sentences.i: And my mind reeled at the sight of it.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ هَذِهِ اَلأَشْيَاءِ أَظُنُّ أَنَّهَا لَا تُوجَدُ فِي خِزَانَةِ مَلِكٍ مِنَ اَلْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu hādhihi l-ashyā'i aẓunnu annahā lā tūjadu fī khizānati malikin mina l-mulūki
sentences.l: And I said, 'These things, I think, are not to be found in the storeroom of a king among kings.'
sentences.i: And I said to myself, 'These things, I think, are not to be found even in the treasury of any king on earth.'

sentences.t: وَانْشَرَحَ حِينَئِذٍ خَاطِرِي وَزَالَ هَمِّي فَقُلْتُ أَنَا اَلْآنَ مَلِكُ عَصْرِي وَهَذِهِ اَلأَمْوَالُ مِنْ فَضْلِ اَللَّهِ عَنْلِي وَ
sentences.tr: wa-inshraḥa ḥīna'idhin khāṭirī wa-zāla hammī fa-qultu anā l-āna maliku ʿaṣrī wa-hādhihi l-amwālu min faḍli llāhi ʿanlī
sentences.l: And my mind was then eased, and my care vanished, and I said, 'I am now the king of my age, and this wealth is from God's bounty ... me.'
sentences.i: And then my heart lifted and my care fell away, and I said, 'I am now a king in my own right, and this wealth is God's bounty upon me...'
sentences.n: Archive prints عنلي (twice in this night, cf. عنلهم just below) where sense calls for عَلَيَّ 'upon me' (parallel عَلَيْهِم 'upon them'); letters kept exactly as printed, vocalised to match the rasm rather than emended, since the consonantal text is not ours to correct.

sentences.t: أَرْبَعُونَ جَارِيَةً تَحْتَ يَدِي وَمَا عَنْلَهُمْ أَحَلُّ غَيْرِي وَلَمْ أَزَلْ
sentences.tr: arbaʿūna jāriyatan taḥta yadī wa-mā ʿanlahum aḥallu ghayrī wa-lam azal
sentences.l: And forty slave-girls are under my hand, and none besides me has more license over them, and I did not cease...
sentences.i: And forty slave-girls were under my command, and no one but I had any claim on them. And I kept on...

sentences.t: أَتَفَرَّجُ مِنْ مَوْضِعٍ إِلَى مَوْضِعٍ حَتَّى مَضَتْ تِسْعَةٌ وَثَلَٰثُونَ يَوْمًا وَ
sentences.tr: atafarraju min mawḍiʿin ilā mawḍiʿin ḥattā maḍat tisʿatun wa-thalāthūna yawman wa
sentences.l: ...going about from place to place, until there passed thirty-nine days.
sentences.i: ...wandering from one place to another, until thirty-nine days had gone by.
sentences.n: ثلثون is the archive's defective (alif-less) spelling of ثلاثون; pointed with a dagger alif so it reads correctly while keeping the printed rasm.

sentences.t: قَٰلَ فَتَحْتُ فِي هَذِهِ اَلْمُدَّةِ اَلْخَزَائِنَ كُلَّهَا إِلَّا اَلْخِزَانَةَ اَلَّتِي مَنَعُونِي
sentences.tr: qāla fataḥtu fī hādhihi l-muddati l-khazā'ina kullahā illā l-khizānata l-latī manaʿūnī
sentences.l: He said: 'I had opened, during this period, all of the storerooms, except the storeroom which they forbade me...'
sentences.i: He went on: 'By this time I had opened every one of the storerooms except the one they had forbidden me...'
sentences.n: قل is the archive's defective spelling of قال; here it functions as the narrator's resumptive tag ('he said'), reintroducing the qalandar's own speech to the lady of the house rather than adding a new speaker. Pointed with a dagger alif, as elsewhere in this edition for such defective spellings.

sentences.t: عَنْ فَتْحِ بَابِهَا فَبَقِيَ خَاطِرِي يَا سَيِّدَتِي مُشْتَغِلًا بِتِلْكَ اَلْخِزَانَةِ اَلَّتِي
sentences.tr: ʿan fatḥi bābihā fa-baqiya khāṭirī yā sayyidatī mushtaghilan bi-tilka l-khizānati l-latī
sentences.l: ...to open its door. And my mind remained, O my lady, occupied with that storeroom which...
sentences.i: ...to open. And my mind, my lady, stayed fixed on that one storeroom, the one that...

sentences.t: هِيَ تَمَامُ أَرْبَعِينَ وَحَكَمَ عَلَيَّ اَلشَّيْطَانُ لِأَجْلِ شَقَاوَتِي بِأَنْ أَفْتَحَهَا
sentences.tr: hiya tamāmu arbaʿīna wa-ḥakama ʿalayya l-shayṭānu li-ajli shaqāwatī bi-an aftaḥahā
sentences.l: ...completes the forty. And Satan decreed over me, for the sake of my wretchedness, that I should open it.
sentences.i: ...made up the full forty. And Satan, to seal my ill fortune, decreed that I would open it.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَجِدْ صَبْرًا عَنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ مِنَ اَلْمِيعَادِ إِلَّا يَوْمٌ وَاحِدٌ فَقُمْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam ajid ṣabran ʿan dhālika wa-lam yabqa mina l-mīʿādi illā yawmun wāḥidun fa-qumtu
sentences.l: And I found no patience to hold back from that, and there remained of the appointed term only one day; so I got up...
sentences.i: I found I could not hold myself back, and only a single day remained of the term. So I rose...

sentences.t: إِلَى اَلْخِزَانَةِ اَلْمَذْكُورَةِ وَفَتَحْتُ بَابَهَا وَدَخَلْتُ فَوَجَدْتُ فِيهَا رَائِحَةً ذَكِيَّةً
sentences.tr: ilā l-khizānati l-madhkūrati wa-fataḥtu bābahā wa-dakhaltu fa-wajadtu fīhā rā'iḥatan dhakiyyatan
sentences.l: ...to the aforementioned storeroom, and I opened its door, and I entered, and I found in it a fragrant scent...
sentences.i: ...to that storeroom, opened its door, and went in — and I found inside a sweet fragrance...

sentences.t: لَمْ أَسْتَرْوِحْ مِثْلَهَا وَخَامَرَتْ عَقْلِي تِلْكَ اَلرَّائِحَةُ فَوَقَعْتُ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَى مِقْدَارَ سَاعَةٍ
sentences.tr: lam astarwiḥ mithlahā wa-khāmarat ʿaqlī tilka l-rā'iḥatu fa-waqaʿtu maghshiyyan ʿalā miqdāra sāʿatin
sentences.l: ...the like of which I had never smelled. And that scent overcame my mind, and I fell in a faint for the space of an hour.
sentences.i: ...unlike anything I had ever smelled. It went straight to my head, and I fell down in a faint for about an hour.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَوَّيْتُ قَلْبِي وَدَخَلْتُ اَلْخِزَانَةَ فَرَأَيْتُ أَرْضَهَا مَفْرُوشَةً
sentences.tr: thumma qawwaytu qalbī wa-dakhaltu l-khizānata fa-ra'aytu arḍahā mafrūshatan
sentences.l: Then I fortified my heart and entered the storeroom, and I saw its floor spread...
sentences.i: Then, steeling myself, I went into the storeroom, and saw its floor strewn...

sentences.t: بِالزَّعْفَرَانِ وَقَنَادِيلَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَمَشْمُومًا يَضُوعُ نَشْرُ اَلْمِسْكِ وَالْعَنْبَرِ مِنْهَا وَهِيَ تَتَّقِدُ نُورًا
sentences.tr: bi-al-zaʿfarāni wa-qanādīla min dhahabin wa-mashmūman yaḍūʿu nashru l-miski wa-al-ʿanbari minhā wa-hiya tattaqidu nūran
sentences.l: ...with saffron, and lamps of gold, and a scented thing from which the fragrance of musk and ambergris wafted, while they blazed with light.
sentences.i: ...with saffron, gold lamps stood about giving off the scent of musk and ambergris, all blazing with light.

sentences.t: وَرَأَيْتُ مِبْخَرَتَيْنِ عَظِيمَتَيْنِ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا مَمْلُوَّةٌ مِنَ اَلْعُودِ وَالْعَنْبَرِ وَالْمُعَسَّلِ وَقَدْ تَعَطَّرَ اَلْمَكَانُ مِنْ عَرَفِهِمَا وَ
sentences.tr: wa-ra'aytu mibkharatayni ʿaẓīmatayni kullu wāḥidatin minhumā mamluwwatun mina l-ʿūdi wa-al-ʿanbari wa-al-muʿassali wa-qad taʿaṭṭara l-makānu min ʿarafihimā wa
sentences.l: And I saw two great censers, each one of them full of aloeswood and ambergris and honeyed [perfume], and the place had grown fragrant from the scent of the two of them.
sentences.i: And I saw two huge censers, each one heaped with aloeswood, ambergris, and a honeyed perfume, and the whole place was scented from them.
sentences.n: مملوة (for مملوءة) drops the hamza letter entirely, a Middle Arabic spelling; pointed to read mamluwwah since no hamza-bearing letter is printed to add a mark to. المعسل ('honeyed') is kept literal; its exact referent (a honey-based perfume paste) is uncertain.

sentences.t: نَظَرْتُ يَا سَيِّدَتِي جَوَادًا أَدْهَمَ كَسَوَادِ اللَّيْلِ إِذَا أَظْلَمَ وَقُدَّامَهُ مِعْلَفٌ
sentences.tr: naẓartu yā sayyidatī jawādan adhama ka-sawādi l-layli idhā aẓlama wa-qudāmahu miʿlafun
sentences.l: And I saw, O my lady, a jet-black horse, like the blackness of night when it grows dark, and before it a manger...
sentences.i: And there, my lady, I saw a horse black as night at its darkest, and before it stood a manger...

sentences.t: مِنَ اَلْبِلَارِ اَلأَبْيَضِ فِيهِ سِمْسِمٌ مَقْشُورٌ وَمِعْلَفٌ آخَرُ مِثْلُهُ فِيهِ مَاءُ وَرْدٍ مُمَسَّكٌ
sentences.tr: mina l-bilāri l-abyaḍi fīhi simsimun maqshūrun wa-miʿlafun ākharu mithluhu fīhi mā'u wardin mumassakun
sentences.l: ...of white crystal, in it husked sesame, and another manger like it, in it musk-scented rose-water.
sentences.i: ...of white crystal, filled with husked sesame, and beside it another manger with musk-scented rose-water.
sentences.n: البلار (for the usual بلور/billawr, 'crystal') is kept as printed; likely a spelling variant rather than an error.

sentences.t: وَالْجَوَادُ مَشْدُودٌ مُلَجَّمٌ وَسَرْجُهُ مِنَ اَلذَّهَبِ اَلأَحْمَرِ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهُ تَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-jawādu mashdūdun mulajjamun wa-sarjuhu mina l-dhahabi l-aḥmari fa-lammā ra'aytuhu taʿajjabtu minhu
sentences.l: And the horse was tethered, bridled, and its saddle was of red gold; and when I saw it, I marveled at it.
sentences.i: The horse stood tethered and bridled, its saddle made of red gold, and when I saw it I was amazed.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي أَنَّ هَذَا لَابُدَّ لَهُ مِنْ شَأْنٍ عَظِيمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu fī nafsī anna hādhā lā budda lahu min sha'nin ʿaẓīmin
sentences.l: And I said to myself, 'This must have some great matter behind it.'
sentences.i: And I said to myself, 'There must be something remarkable about this.'

sentences.t: وَأَضَلَّنِي اَلشَّيْطَانُ فَأَخْرَجْتُهُ وَرَكِبْتُهُ فَلَمْ يَبْرَحْ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ فَرَفَسْتُهُ فَلَمْ يَتَحَرَّكْ
sentences.tr: wa-aḍallanī l-shayṭānu fa-akhrajtuhu wa-rakibtuhu fa-lam yabraḥ min makānihi fa-rafastuhu fa-lam yataḥarrak
sentences.l: And Satan led me astray, so I brought it out and mounted it; but it did not stir from its place, so I kicked it, but it did not move.
sentences.i: Satan led me astray: I brought it out and mounted it, but it would not budge, so I kicked it, and still it did not move.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ اَلْمِقْرَعَةَ وَضَرَبْتُهُ بِهَا فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ بِالضَّرْبَةِ صَهَلَ صُرَاخًا بِصَوْتٍ كَالرَّعْدِ اَلْقَاصِفِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu l-miqraʿata wa-ḍarabtuhu bihā fa-lammā aḥassa bi-al-ḍarbati ṣahala ṣurākhan bi-ṣawtin ka-al-raʿdi l-qāṣifi
sentences.l: So I took the whip and struck it with it; and when it felt the blow, it neighed a scream with a voice like crashing thunder.
sentences.i: So I took up the whip and struck it, and the moment it felt the blow it let out a neighing scream like the crash of thunder.

sentences.t: وَفَتَحَ لَهُ جَنَاحَيْنِ فَطَارَ بِي وَ غَابَ عَنِ اَلْأَبْصَارِ فِي جَوِّ اَلسَّمَاءِ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: wa-fataḥa lahu janāḥayni fa-ṭāra bī wa ghāba ʿani l-abṣāri fī jawwi l-samā'i sāʿatan
sentences.l: And two wings opened for it, and it flew off with me, and vanished from sight in the vault of the sky for an hour.
sentences.i: Two wings opened out on it, and it flew off carrying me, and we vanished from every eye into the sky for a full hour.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَطَّنِي عَلَى سَطْحٍ وَ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥaṭṭanī ʿalā saṭḥin wa-
sentences.l: Then it set me down on a rooftop, and — [the sentence continues beyond this slice]
sentences.i: Then it set me down on a rooftop, and — [continues into the next slice]
sentences.n: This excerpt breaks off mid-sentence, on the dangling conjunction وَ; the clause it introduces continues past this point.

sentences.t: أَنْزَلَنِي وَنَشَّنِي بِذَيْلِهِ عَلَى وَجْهِي قَلَعَ عَيْنِي الْيُمْنَى وَسَيَّلَهَا عَلَى خَدِّي وَذَهَبَ عَنِّي
sentences.tr: anzalanī wa-nashshanī bi-dhaylihi ʿalā wajhī qalaʿa ʿaynī al-yumnā wa-sayyalahā ʿalā khaddī wa-dhahaba ʿannī
sentences.l: He set-me-down and wiped-me with his hem/tail upon my face; he plucked my eye, the right(-one), and made-it-flow upon my cheek; and he went away from me.
sentences.i: He set me down and wiped my face with the hem of his garment; he plucked out my right eye and let it run down my cheek — and then he was gone.
sentences.n: This continues a sentence begun earlier: the unnamed 'he' is whatever unseen hand seized the qalandar on the rooftop after he mounted the black horse from the fortieth storeroom (told earlier in the night). نَشَّنِي is printed exactly thus (root ن-ش-ش); Classical dictionaries know نَشَّ mainly of water drying up, not of a transitive 'wipe/dry X', so the sense taken here — 'wiped, mopped' — is the best fit for the context but genuinely uncertain, and is admitted as such rather than resolved.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلْتُ مِنْ عَلَى السَّطْحِ فَوَجَدْتُ الْعَشَرَةَ شَبَابَ الْعُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazaltu min ʿalā al-saṭḥi fa-wajadtu al-ʿasharata shabāba al-ʿūr
sentences.l: So I came down from off the roof, and I found the ten, young-men-of the one-eyed.
sentences.i: So I climbed down from the roof, and there I found the ten one-eyed young men.
sentences.n: These are the ten one-eyed young men whose palace he reached earlier tonight, after the rukh set him down and before the black horse threw him up onto this roof; the number is given here explicitly as ten.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لِي لَا مَرْحَبًا بِكَ وَلَا أَهْلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lī lā marḥaban bika wa-lā ahlan
sentences.l: So they said to me: 'No welcome to you, and no greeting.'
sentences.i: And they said to me: 'No welcome to you, and no greeting.'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ هَا أَنَا قَدْ صِرْتُ وَاحِدًا مِثْلَكُمْ وَأَشْتَهِي تُعْطُونِي طَاقَةَ السَّوَادِ أَسْتَمُّ بِهَا وَجْهِي وَتَجْعَلُونِي أَجْلِسُ عِنْدَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahum hā anā qad ṣirtu wāḥidan mithlakum wa-ashtahī tuʿṭūnī ṭāqata al-sawādi astammu bihā wajhī wa-tajʿalūnī ajlisu ʿindakum
sentences.l: So I said to them: 'Here I am — I have become one like you, and I desire [that] you give me a lump of the black(-soot), [that] I astammu with it my face, and [that] you let me sit among you.'
sentences.i: So I said to them: 'Here I am, become one of you; I ask only that you give me a bit of the soot to blacken my face with, and let me sit among you.'
sentences.n: Twice here a complement clause follows a verb of wishing with no أَنْ: tuʿṭūnī and ajlisu are both plain indicatives standing in for a subjunctive 'that you give / that I sit'. The verb printed استم (four letters, ا-س-ت-م) matches no attested root: it is vocalized here as أَسْتَمُّ purely to make it pronounceable, and the sense 'blacken' is supplied from context (the ash-ritual), not from a secure derivation — a genuine crux, admitted as such rather than resolved.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا وَاللَّهِ لَا تَجْلِسُ عِنْدَنَا وَاخْرُجْ مِنْ هُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālū wa-Allāhi lā tajlisu ʿindanā wa-ukhruj min hunā
sentences.l: But they said: 'By God, you shall not sit with us — get out from here!'
sentences.i: But they said: 'By God, you shall not sit with us — get out of here!'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَرَدُونِي وَضَاقَ لِي الْأَمْرُ وَافْتَكَرْتُ عَلَى مَاجَرَى عَلَى نَاصِيَتِي خَرَجْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ حَزِينَ الْقَلْبِ بَاكِيَ الْعَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭaradūnī wa-ḍāqa lī al-amru wa-iftakartu ʿalā mā jarā ʿalā nāṣiyatī kharajtu min ʿindihim ḥazīna al-qalbi bākiya al-ʿayn
sentences.l: And when they drove me away, and the matter grew narrow for me, and I reflected upon what had befallen my forelock, I went out from among them, sad of heart, weeping of eye.
sentences.i: When they drove me away, and the whole matter weighed heavy on me, and I turned over in my mind what fate had written on my very brow, I went out from among them with a sorrowful heart and weeping eyes.
sentences.n: نَاصِيَة, literally 'forelock', is the idiomatic seat of a man's fortune in this prose — 'what had befallen my forelock' means simply 'what fate had dealt me'. حَزِينَ الْقَلْبِ and بَاكِيَ الْعَيْنِ are accusatives of state describing the speaker as he left.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ خَفِيفَةً كُنْتُ قَاعِدًا بِطُولِي فَمَا خَلَّانِي فُضُولِي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu khafīfatan kuntu qāʿidan bi-ṭūlī fa-mā khallānī fuḍūlī
sentences.l: And I said [the saying]: 'Light-at-ease I was, sitting at my full length, but my own inquisitiveness would not leave me be.'
sentences.i: And I said to myself: 'I was living easy, minding my own business — but my own curiosity would not let me alone.'
sentences.n: A little rhymed saying inserted in the speech, on the sajʿ pattern of this prose: بِطُولِي rhymes with فُضُولِي (-ūlī).

sentences.t: فَحَلَقْتُ ذَقْنِي وَشَوَارِبِي وَطُفْتُ فِي بِلَادِ اللَّهِ وَكَتَبَ اللَّهُ لِي السَّلَامَةَ حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ فِي مَسَاءِ هَٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥalaqtu dhaqnī wa-shawāribī wa-ṭuftu fī bilādi Allāhi wa-kataba Allāhu lī al-salāmata ḥattā waṣaltu ilā Baghdāda fī masāʾi hādhihi al-layla
sentences.l: So I shaved my chin and my mustaches, and I wandered in the lands of God, and God decreed for me safety, until I arrived at Baghdad in the evening of this night.
sentences.i: So I shaved my chin and my mustaches, and wandered through God's lands, and God ordained my safety, until I came to Baghdad this very evening.

sentences.t: فَأَجِدُ هَؤُلَاءِ الِاثْنَيْنِ الْوَاقِفَيْنِ حَائِرَيْنِ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ قُلْتُ أَنَا غَرِيبٌ فَقَالُوا وَنَحْنُ أَيْضًا غُرَبَاءُ
sentences.tr: fa-ajidu hāʾulāʾi al-ithnayni al-wāqifayni ḥāʾirayni fa-sallamtu ʿalayhim wa-qultu anā gharībun fa-qālū wa-naḥnu ayḍan ghurabāʾ
sentences.l: And I find these two, the two standing-ones, the two bewildered — so I greeted them, and said, 'I am a stranger.' And they said, 'And we too are strangers.'
sentences.i: And there I find these two men standing about, at a loss — so I greeted them, and said, 'I am a stranger here.' 'And so are we,' they said.
sentences.n: فَأَجِدُ slips into the vivid present tense for a moment inside a past-tense narration, as if the speaker were reliving the encounter as he tells it.

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقْنَا نَحْنُ الثَّلٰثَةُ الْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةُ عُورٌ مِنَ الْيَمِينِ وَهَٰذَا يَا سَيِّدَتِي سَبَبُ حَلْقِ ذَقْنِي وَقَلْعِ عَيْنِي
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqnā naḥnu al-thalāthatu al-qarandaliyyatu ʿūrun mina al-yamīni wa-hādhā yā sayyidatī sababu ḥalqi dhaqnī wa-qalʿi ʿaynī
sentences.l: And we agreed, we three, the qalandars, one-eyed from the right — and this, my lady, is the reason for the shaving of my chin and the plucking-out of my eye.
sentences.i: And so we three qalandars, each blind in the right eye, fell in together — and this, my lady, is the reason my chin is shaved and my eye put out.
sentences.n: الثَّلٰثَة is printed الثلثة, missing the medial alif of الثلاثة; pointed here with a dagger alif, as قل is pointed for قال. This closes the Third Qalandar's own tale.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَلِّسْ عَلَى رَأْسِكَ وَرُحْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu mallis ʿalā raʾsika wa-ruḥ
sentences.l: So she said to him: 'Stroke your head, and go.'
sentences.i: So she said to him: 'Let it be, and go your way.'
sentences.n: مَلِّسْ عَلَى رَأْسِكَ وَرُحْ — literally 'stroke your head and go' — is a dismissive idiom of resignation, close to 'shrug it off and be on your way'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَرُوحُ حَتَّى أَسْمَعَ قِصَّةَ هَؤُلَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi lā arūḥu ḥattā asmaʿa qiṣṣata hāʾulāʾ
sentences.l: But he said: 'By God, I will not go until I hear the story of these.'
sentences.i: But he said: 'By God, I will not leave until I have heard the story of these two.'
sentences.n: 'These' are the two black bitches and the doorkeeper-sister, whose story is still owed from earlier in the night.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الصَّبِيَّةَ اِلْتَفَتَتْ إِلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ وَجَعْفَرٍ وَمَسْرُورٍ وَ قَالَتْ لَهُمُ احْكُوا لِي عَلَى خَبَرِكُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ṣabiyyata iltafatat ilā al-khalīfati wa-Jaʿfarin wa-Masrūrin wa-qālat lahumu iḥkū lī ʿalā khabarikum
sentences.l: Then indeed the young lady turned to the caliph, and Jaʿfar, and Masrūr, and said to them: 'Tell me your story.'
sentences.i: Then the lady of the house turned to the caliph, Jaʿfar, and Masrūr, and said: 'Tell me your story.'
sentences.n: 'The young lady' is the mistress of the house, still unaware that the merchant before her is the caliph himself.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ جَعْفَرٌ وَحَكَى لَهَا الْحِكَايَةَ الَّتِي قَالَهَا لِلْبَوَّابَةِ عِنْدَ دُخُولِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama Jaʿfarun wa-ḥakā lahā al-ḥikāyata allatī qālahā li-al-bawwābati ʿinda dukhūlihim
sentences.l: So Jaʿfar came forward and told her the story that he had told the doorkeeper-sister at their entering.
sentences.i: So Jaʿfar stepped forward and repeated to her the story he had told the portress when they first came in.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ قَالَتْ وَهَبْتُكُمْ لِبَعْضِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu qālat wahabtukum li-baʿḍikum
sentences.l: And when she heard his words, she said: 'I have granted you to one another.'
sentences.i: And when she heard him out, she said: 'I forgive you all, for one another's sake.'

sentences.t: فَخَرَجُوا إِلَى أَنْ صَارُوا فِي الزُّقَاقِ فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لِلْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةِ يَا جَمَاعَةُ أَيْنَ أَنْتُمْ قَاصِدِينَ الْآنَ وَالْفَجْرُ مَا لَاحَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajū ilā an ṣārū fī al-zuqāqi fa-qāla al-khalīfatu li-al-qarandaliyyati yā jamāʿatu ayna antum qāṣidīna al-āna wa-al-fajru mā lāḥ
sentences.l: So they went out, until they were in the lane; and the caliph said to the qalandars: 'O company, where are you headed now, the dawn not having yet appeared?'
sentences.i: So they all went out into the lane; and the caliph said to the qalandars: 'Good people, where are you bound for now, with dawn not yet broken?'

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا وَاللَّهِ يَا سَيِّدَنَا لَا نَدْرِي إِلَى أَيْنَ نَذْهَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū wa-Allāhi yā sayyidanā lā nadrī ilā ayna nadhhab
sentences.l: They said: 'By God, our lord, we do not know to where we are going.'
sentences.i: 'By God, good sir,' they said, 'we do not know where we are going.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْخَلِيفَةُ سِيرُوا وَبَاتُوا عِنْدَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-khalīfatu sīrū wa-bātū ʿindanā
sentences.l: So the caliph said to them: 'Come along, and spend the night with us.'
sentences.i: So the caliph said to them: 'Come with us, and spend what is left of the night as our guests.'

sentences.t: وَ قَالَ لِجَعْفَرٍ خُذْهُمْ وَأَحْضِرْهُمْ لِي غَدًا نُؤَرِّخُ مَا جَرَى فَامْتَثَلَ جَعْفَرٌ مَا أَمَرَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-Jaʿfarin khudhhum wa-aḥḍirhum lī ghadan nuʾarrikhu mā jarā fa-imtathala Jaʿfarun mā amara lahu al-khalīfa
sentences.l: And he said to Jaʿfar: 'Take them, and bring them to me tomorrow — we will set down in writing what has happened.' So Jaʿfar carried out what the caliph had ordered him.
sentences.i: And he said to Jaʿfar: 'Take charge of them, and bring them before me tomorrow, so that we may put on record what has happened.' And Jaʿfar did as the caliph had bidden him.
sentences.n: نُؤَرِّخُ, 'we shall date/record', follows without a linking particle, as a plain purpose clause — again the loose, particle-less subordination this prose favours.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ طَلَعَ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ وَلَمْ يَعْتَرِهِ مَنَامٌ فِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata ṭalaʿa ilā qaṣrihi wa-lam yaʿtarihi manāmun fī tilka al-layla
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph went up to his palace, and no sleep visited him that night.
sentences.i: Then the caliph withdrew to his palace, and that night no sleep came to him at all.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ جَلَسَ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ الْمَمْلَكَةِ وَاِلْتَفَتَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ بَعْدَ أَنْ طَلَعَ أَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu jalasa ʿalā kursiyyi al-mamlakati wa-iltafata ilā Jaʿfarin baʿda an ṭalaʿa arbābu al-dawla
sentences.l: And when morning came, he sat upon the throne of the kingdom, and turned to Jaʿfar, after the lords of the state had come up.
sentences.i: And when morning broke, he took his seat upon the throne, and, once the great men of the realm had come in to attend him, turned to Jaʿfar.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ ائْتِنِي بِالثَّلٰثَةِ صَبَايَا وَالْكَلْبَتَيْنِ وَالْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةِ فَنَهَضَ جَعْفَرٌ وَأَحْضَرَهُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla iʾtinī bi-al-thalāthati ṣabāyā wa-al-kalbatayni wa-al-qarandaliyyati fa-nahaḍa Jaʿfarun wa-aḥḍarahum bayna yadayh
sentences.l: And he said: 'Bring me the three young ladies, and the two she-dogs, and the qalandars.' So Jaʿfar rose and brought them before him.
sentences.i: And he said: 'Bring me the three sisters, the two bitches, and the qalandars.' So Jaʿfar rose and brought them all into his presence.

sentences.t: فَأَدْخَلَ الصَّبَايَا تَحْتَ الْأَسْتَارِ وَاِلْتَفَتَ لَهُمْ جَعْفَرٌ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ قَدْ عَفَوْنَا عَنْكُمْ بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَيْنَا وَلَمْ تَعْرِفُونَا
sentences.tr: fa-adkhala al-ṣabāyā taḥta al-astāri wa-iltafata lahum Jaʿfarun wa-qāla lahum qad ʿafawnā ʿankum bimā aslaftum mina al-iḥsāni ilaynā wa-lam taʿrifūnā
sentences.l: So he brought the young ladies in behind the curtains, and Jaʿfar turned to them and said to them: 'We have [already] pardoned you for the kindness you showed beforehand toward us, when you did not know us.'
sentences.i: He had the three sisters brought in behind a screen, and Jaʿfar turned to the qalandars and said: 'We have already forgiven you the kindness you once did us, not knowing who we were.'

sentences.t: فَهَا أَنَا أُعَرِّفُكُمْ أَنْتُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الْخَامِسِ مِنْ بَنِى الْعَبَّاسِ الْهَارُونِ الرَّشِيدِ أَخْ مُوسَي الْهَادِي بْنِ الْمَهْدِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ بْنِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْمَنْصُورِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ أَخْ السَّفَّاحِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-hā anā uʿarrifukum antum bayna yadayi al-khāmisi min banī al-ʿAbbāsi al-Hārūni al-Rashīdi akh Mūsā al-Hādī bni al-Mahdiyyi Muḥammadin bni Abī Jaʿfarin al-Manṣūri bni Muḥammadin akh al-Saffāḥi bni Muḥammad
sentences.l: So here — I make known to you: you stand before the fifth of the sons of al-ʿAbbās, Hārūn al-Rashīd, brother of Mūsā al-Hādī son of al-Mahdī Muḥammad son of Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr son of Muḥammad, brother of al-Saffāḥ son of Muḥammad.
sentences.i: 'Now let me tell you: you stand before the fifth of the sons of al-ʿAbbās — Hārūn al-Rashīd, brother of al-Hādī Mūsā, son of al-Mahdī Muḥammad, son of Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr, son of Muḥammad, brother of al-Saffāḥ, son of Muḥammad.'
sentences.n: The genealogy hangs entirely on أَخْ, printed twice as the bare two letters اخ with none of the case-marking long vowel that 'brother' normally takes in construct (أَخُو / أَخَا / أَخِي) — the five special nouns are simply frozen here as invariable أَخْ, a common Middle Arabic levelling. أُعَرِّفُكُمْ is read as Form II 'I make known to you' rather than Form I 'I know you', since Jaʿfar is revealing an identity, not stating a fact of recognition.

sentences.t: فَلَا تُخْبِرُوهُ إِلَّا حَقًّا
sentences.tr: fa-lā tukhbirūhu illā ḥaqqan
sentences.l: So tell him nothing but the truth.
sentences.i: So tell him nothing but the truth.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الصَّبَايَا كَلَامَ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ لِسَانِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ تَقَدَّمَتِ الْكَبِيرَةُ وَقَالَتْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-ṣabāyā kalāma Jaʿfarin ʿan lisāni amīri al-muʾminīna taqaddamati al-kabīratu wa-qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīn
sentences.l: And when the young ladies heard Jaʿfar's words on behalf of the Commander of the Faithful, the eldest came forward and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful,
sentences.i: And when the three sisters heard, from Jaʿfar's own mouth, that they stood before the Commander of the Faithful, the eldest of them came forward and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful,

sentences.t: لِي حَدِيثٌ لَوْ كُتِبَ بِالْإِبَرِ عَلَى آمَاقِ الْبَصَرِ لَصَارَ عِبْرَةً لِمَنِ اعْتَبَرَ وَنَصِيحَةً لِمَنْ يَنْتَصِحُ
sentences.tr: lī ḥadīthun law kutiba bi-al-ibari ʿalā āmāqi al-baṣari la-ṣāra ʿibratan li-mani iʿtabara wa-naṣīḥatan li-man yantaṣiḥ
sentences.l: I have a story that, if it were written with needles upon the corners of the eye, would become a lesson for whoever takes heed, and a counsel for whoever seeks counsel.
sentences.i: I have a tale that, were it written in needles on the very corners of the eyes, would stand as a lesson to whoever heeds it, and a counsel to whoever seeks counsel.'

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalām
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, so she fell silent, and ceased from speaking.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent.
